subject: Next steps: prompt harvest, redaction guidance, and eval benchmark links
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Thomas <aisha.thomas@lumoshealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: prompt harvest, redaction guidance, and eval benchmark links

Hi Aisha — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of call
- Use-case: internal clinical triage assistant for intake clerks (answerer + rewrite) with conservative hallucination guardrails.
- Primary success metrics you shared: 95% safe/accurate triage suggestions; <300ms median token latency for single-turn assist; unit cost target ~$0.0008/token.
- Data constraints: patient-identifiable fields will be redacted; retention policy 90 days for prompt logs.

Redwood recommendations (shortlist)
- For initial eval: redwood/turbine-7b-q4f — good latency/cost balance for triage prompts.
- For higher-quality fallbacks (canary stage): llama-2-13b-q4f or redwood/zen-13b (if you want better long-tail accuracy).
- We can provide token-cost/latency projections per model against a 25k prompt sample once we have your sample set.

What we need from you (asks)
1) Prompt set: ~200–300 de-identified prompts across the main flows (intake question, symptom rewrite, short summary). Include 10–20 edge cases (ambiguous symptoms, code words, mixed language). CSV template attached (lumos_prompt_sample_batch.csv).
2) Labeling: flag any prompt that may contain PHI/PII in a "sensitive" column; if you cannot fully redact, replace with [REDACTED].
3) Privacy question: please confirm the retention window and whether we should exclude any org IDs or job titles from samples.

Links & artifacts
- Benchmark starter sheet: https://drive.redwood.com/benchmarks/lumos-health-eval-2027
- Internal redaction best-practices (summary attached): redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf

Next actions
- Aisha: share initial ~50 sample prompts by EOD Friday to unblock a rapid smoke test.
- Redwood (me + Karthik): run a quick 50-sample run and return quality/regression notes + model/cost estimates by Tue.

Attachments: lumos_prompt_sample_batch.csv (CSV template, columns: id, prompt_text, flow, sensitive_flag, notes)

Thanks — happy to hop back on a short call if you want to walk through the template.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

From: Aisha Thomas <aisha.thomas@lumoshealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: LumosHealth Data Team <data@lumoshealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: prompt harvest, redaction guidance, and eval benchmark links

Thanks Sergio — helpful recap. Quick answers and next steps from our side: 

- We'll extract an initial 50 prompts from live intake logs (de-identified) and validate redaction per your guidance. Expect that file by Friday COB.
- Retention: Lumos retains raw logs 180 days; for the eval set we prefer to share only de-identified prompts and metadata. Legal asked us to confirm that Redwood will not persist any unredacted records — can you confirm?
- On edge cases: we'll include a few examples with non-English snippets (Spanish) and one or two examples with shorthand codes clinicians use.

Attaching: lumos_sample_extract.csv (first 20 rows). This is redacted locally; some clinician initials remain — please treat those as sensitive.

A couple quick questions: 
1) Do you have a short checklist we should follow to tag prompts as sensitive vs acceptable?
2) If we need to share anything under NDA for full logs, who on your team handles secure uploads?

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Thomas
Head of Data Products | LumosHealth
aisha.thomas@lumoshealth.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Thomas <aisha.thomas@lumoshealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: prompt harvest, redaction guidance, and eval benchmark links

Aisha — thanks, got the sample extract. Quick answers inline and a couple of concrete next actions: 

Legal / retention / storage
- Short answer: for the quick eval we will not persist unredacted records. Redwood's smoke test environment will only retain the de-identified payloads you send and temporary logs for 30 days (we'll mirror your retention preference if you want 90/180 days; we can also set up a Private deployment with customer-managed KMS if you require stricter controls).
- If you prefer secure upload under NDA, please send me the legal contact; we will route to our security team and provide a secure SFTP/portal link.

Redaction checklist (high level) — also attaching internal doc: redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf
- Replace direct PII with [REDACTED] tokens (names, MRNs, phone, SSN).
- For clinical shorthand: either expand in a separate column or mark as "ambig_shorthand" so we can treat as an edge-case.
- DO NOT remove clinical content that affects model behavior (symptom strings, durations).

Model + eval note (practical tradeoffs)
- For the 50-sample smoke run we'll test: redwood/turbine-7b-q4f (fast), and a tuned 13b variant (bench only).
- Expected median per-request latency (50-sample, 128-token context): turbine-7b-q4f ~220ms; 13b ~480ms. Estimated unit cost (prompt+25 tok output): turbine ~$0.0006/token, 13b ~$0.0018/token. These are preliminary and will be updated after the sample run.

Next actions (revised)
- Aisha: upload 50 de-identified prompts + flag column for sensitive items (thanks for the extract).
- Sergio + Karthik: run smoke test and return a short quality report + suggested model picks and quantization profile by Tue morning.
- Karthik: I'll let you add the prompt-tag schema and capture template in a separate note.

Attachments: redaction_guidelines_v1.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min technical sync if your engineering team wants to review the sample schema.

Best,
Sergio

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Thomas <aisha.thomas@lumoshealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: Prompt tagging schema & quick capture template

Hi Aisha — quick note from the SE side with the minimal tagging schema we'd like to consume. Keeping it intentionally small to reduce lift on your side.

Prompt capture columns (recommended):
- id (unique)
- flow (intake | rewrite | summary)
- prompt_text (the user text)
- sensitive_flag (none | pii | phi | ambig_shorthand)
- language (en | es | other)
- expected_output_type (short_answer | rewrite | summary)
- notes (free text; call out any special clinician shorthand)

Edge-case categories to include (please include at least one example of each if possible):
- ambiguous symptoms ("pain in chest vs indigestion")
- multilingual fragments (Spanish + English)
- codewords/shorthand (clinician abbreviations)
- prompt injection (e.g., pasted clinician instructions that could confuse system)
- long context examples (>250 tokens)

I've attached a small template: prompt_capture_template.xlsx (two sample rows). Once you upload the 50, we'll run the smoke test and share the annotation/quality highlights.

If anyone on the Lumos engineering side wants to pair for 30 minutes I can walk through the upload process and the secure-transfer options.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
